packages.name: Mathematics · calculation & geometry
packages.description: Selected written mathematical evidence, kept separate from the algebra package. Counting and practical mathematics are much older than the surviving texts shown here; these are not invention dates.

attestations.name: Early Egyptian writing at Abydos
attestations.summary: Inscribed objects from Tomb U-j are among Egypt’s earliest writing evidence. Short early sign groups differ from the continuous prose attested much later.
attestations.location_note: Approximate cemetery vicinity, not a surveyed tomb coordinate.

attestations.name: Developed Indus script at Harappa
attestations.summary: Developed Indus inscriptions are attested by the Mature Harappan period. Earlier marks and inscriptions have disputed definitions and chronology; this entry does not assign them a precise origin date. The script remains undeciphered.
attestations.location_note: Site-level anchor. Earlier signs elsewhere are not excluded by this conservative entry.

attestations.name: Linear B administrative records
attestations.summary: Linear B documents attest Greek in Bronze Age Crete and mainland Greece. This broad corpus interval is not a precise date for a particular Knossos tablet, and earlier Aegean writing traditions are not represented by this entry.
attestations.location_note: Knossos is one corpus location; the date interval describes the wider corpus, not continuous occupation or literacy here.

attestations.name: Early Maya writing at San Bartolo
attestations.evidence: painted glyphs with associated dated charcoal
attestations.summary: A painted glyph sample is associated with charcoal dated to this interval. It is early Maya evidence, not the first writing in all Mesoamerica; other scripts and earlier claims require separate entries.
attestations.location_note: Approximate archaeological-site anchor; the dates are for associated material, not a direct measurement of the paint.

attestations.name: Commius coin inscriptions before Roman conquest
attestations.summary: The British Museum identifies coinage naming Commius as probably Britain’s earliest writing evidence. Coin inscriptions precede the surviving Roman handwritten documents. This is a qualified museum interpretation, not a claim that writing was absent earlier.
attestations.location_note: Illustrative southern-English anchor, not an excavated mint or a particular coin’s findspot.

attestations.name: Roman London’s early writing tablets
attestations.summary: MOLA reports a tablet dated archaeologically to 43–53 CE and a separate financial document explicitly dated 8 January 57 CE. These establish early handwritten documents in Roman London, rather than Britain’s first use of writing.
attestations.location_note: Excavation-area anchor. The mapped record is the earlier archaeological interval, not the exact-date 57 CE document.

attestations.name: Moscow Mathematical Papyrus
attestations.summary: The Moscow Papyrus is one of the early surviving Egyptian mathematical texts. Its approximate date does not establish the beginning of mathematics in Egypt.
attestations.location_note: Egyptian regional anchor; no secure production location is assigned, and the modern museum location is not mapped.

attestations.name: Old Babylonian square-root calculation
attestations.summary: YBC 7289 records a highly accurate approximation of the square root of two. This surviving exercise is not the earliest calculation in Mesopotamia, nor evidence of universal mathematical education.
attestations.location_note: Illustrative regional anchor; the tablet has no securely assigned excavation findspot. Its current Yale collection location is not its place of production.

attestations.name: Suan shu shu · Writings on Reckoning
attestations.summary: A mathematical collection was recovered from a tomb thought to have closed in 186 BCE. The date is a latest bound for deposition, not a known composition year or the beginning of Chinese mathematics.
attestations.location_note: Approximate tomb-site vicinity; the manuscript’s place of composition is not established.

arce-early-writing.title: Demotic: The History, Development and Techniques of Ancient Egypt’s Popular Script
arce-early-writing.author: Steve Vinson, Indiana University; American Research Center in Egypt
arce-early-writing.locator: Opening discussion: early writing in Tomb U-j at Abydos around 3200 BCE; continuous prose developed later.

harappa-writing-experts.title: How old is the oldest ancient Indus writing?
harappa-writing-experts.author: Asko Parpola, Jonathan Mark Kenoyer and other researchers, Harappa.com
harappa-writing-experts.locator: Expert answers distinguish precursors, Early Harappan inscriptions and developed script in 2600–1900 BCE; definitions differ.

oslo-linear-b.title: The Mycenaean Documents
oslo-linear-b.author: DĀMOS, University of Oslo
oslo-linear-b.locator: Corpus introduction: administrative texts c.1450–1150 BCE from Crete and mainland Greek palaces. Factual summary only; no corpus text imported.

saturno-san-bartolo.title: Early Maya writing at San Bartolo, Guatemala
saturno-san-bartolo.author: William A. Saturno, David Stuart and Boris Beltrán, Science 311, 2006
saturno-san-bartolo.locator: Abstract: associated charcoal has calibrated radiocarbon dates of 200–300 BCE; this is Maya evidence, not an all-Mesoamerican first.

bm-commius-writing.title: Money gallery · Room 68 large print guide
bm-commius-writing.author: British Museum, 2020
bm-commius-writing.locator: Search Commius: southern England, about 40–25 BCE; coin probably the earliest writing evidence in Britain.

mola-bloomberg-writing.title: Archaeological research into Britain’s oldest hand-written documents released
mola-bloomberg-writing.author: MOLA · Museum of London Archaeology
mola-bloomberg-writing.locator: Highlights: one tablet archaeologically dated 43–53 CE; a different financial document dated 8 January 57 CE.

ou-egyptian-maths.title: Egyptian mathematics · Mathematics in Egyptian history
ou-egyptian-maths.author: The Open University, OpenLearn
ou-egyptian-maths.locator: Section 1.1: Moscow/Golenischev papyrus dated approximately 1850 BCE, distinguished from Rhind papyrus.

fowler-robson-ybc.title: Square root approximations in Old Babylonian mathematics: YBC 7289 in context
fowler-robson-ybc.author: David Fowler and Eleanor Robson, Historia Mathematica 25, 1998
fowler-robson-ybc.locator: Study of YBC 7289 and its Old Babylonian mathematical context; regional anchor, not an excavated origin claim.

cullen-reckoning.title: The Suan shu shu · Writings on Reckoning
cullen-reckoning.author: Christopher Cullen, Needham Research Institute, Working Paper 1, 2004
cullen-reckoning.locator: Introduction: mathematical text on bamboo recovered at Zhangjiashan; documentary evidence places tomb closure around 186 BCE.
